name: RareArena
intro: RareArena 是一个覆盖近 5 万名患者、4000 多种疾病的罕见病诊断基准，包含罕见病筛查和罕见病确认两类任务，用于评估模型在真实病例基础上的诊断召回能力。
intro_en: RareArena is a rare-disease diagnosis benchmark covering nearly 50,000 patients and more than 4,000 diseases. It includes rare-disease screening and confirmation settings to evaluate diagnostic recall on real patient cases.

drawio_review_note: reviewed_at=2026-07-18; status=source-reconstructed-awaiting-independent-signoff. Primary paper evidence is the open-access Lancet Digital Health Resource article, DOI 10.1016/j.landig.2025.100953, published in volume 8 issue 2 in 2026. It was cross-checked against the official zhao-zy15/RareArena repository at current revision 80e16b1438729562b19c3b3103a31ac9f4949048 and against the paper-era repository history. Paper construction starts from the June 2024 PubMed Central release of 5.8 million articles. The authors reproduce the PMC-Patients extraction approach, identify candidate case-report paragraphs with regular expressions, and obtain 250,294 candidate cases. Three medical experts manually review candidates to design comprehensive diagnostic-focus rules; GPT-4o-2024-05-13 applies the filters and extracts final diagnoses. The rules cover one human patient, diagnosis after birth and before death, a clear single outcome, diagnostic rather than treatment focus, and exclusion of unsuitable special situations. After filtering, 104,000 cases remain. The extracted final diagnosis, not the later Orphanet concept, is retained as the gold label. Mapping uses CODER embeddings to retrieve the ten most similar Orphanet disease terms by cosine similarity; GPT-4o selects a valid mapping and cases without adequate mapping are removed. This yields 57,000 mapped diagnoses. A manual audit of 100 mappings reports 94% accuracy. The pipeline then identifies diagnostic tests that directly confirm or strongly suggest the diagnosis and cleans their results. RDS and RDC must remain separate. Rare Disease Screening truncates the narrative immediately before any diagnostic test, retains symptoms and routine examinations, and may include cases without a specific diagnostic test. Rare Disease Confirmation truncates immediately before the final diagnosis, includes cleaned diagnostic-test findings, and requires a specific diagnostic test. GPT-4o rephrases each case to retain factual clinical findings while removing subjective analysis, suspected diagnoses, decision rationales, and diagnosis cues. A separate leakage detector checks literal diagnosis names, synonyms, and abbreviations; potential leakage is discarded, and RDS also excludes leaking test-result cues. The paper releases 49,760 RDS cases covering 4,597 diseases and 22,901 RDC cases covering 3,522 diseases. Human quality evaluation is part of the validation path: two physicians independently score 100 randomly selected cases, 50 from each task, after calibrating on ten joint cases; a third reviewer adjudicates disagreements. The three quality dimensions are diagnosis leakage, generation fidelity, and clinical complexity. Benchmark models receive the same zero-shot prompt, return the five most likely rare-disease diagnoses, and use temperature 0.1 in the paper protocol. This is the primary full-benchmark regime used for the headline RDS and RDC results. A separate prompt-method analysis uses a random 500-case subset to compare chain-of-thought and few-shot prompting. Few-shot uses three fixed randomly selected demonstrations that are disjoint from the 500 analyzed cases. GPT-4o aligns each candidate to the gold diagnosis with score 2 for a synonym or exact equivalent, score 1 for a hypernym, and score 0 for a miss. Top-1 and Top-5 recall count either score 1 or score 2 as retrieved and are reported separately for RDS and RDC. Release and implementation boundaries are explicit. The original data commit is 4a822f1f9c992adca6d90221537f50dc2b05a399 dated 2024-11-03; reproduction scripts were added at f8dc1fb2c08826259911cc45b71435d2f0d7b898 dated 2025-04-09; the paper-era evaluator update is b18bc13492d9e8999cb143c9db31ac29bd3fd12e dated 2025-04-22. The current 2026 head adds a stricter Orphanet-hypernym evaluator and representative sampled subsets; these are post-paper drift, not replacements for the paper snapshot. Direct line counts at the pinned current head are RDS 8,562 cases across 3,727 disease IDs and RDC 4,376 cases across 2,644 disease IDs, distinct from the paper-scale releases. The official repository and paper data-sharing statement declare CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 for the dataset on GitHub and Hugging Face. The bilingual specs use solid arrows only for the paper pipeline and dashed arrows for evidence, mapping audit, release history, post-paper code and subset drift, and licensing. No post-paper sampled count or evaluator rule is injected into the paper scoring path. This is source-stage evidence only. strict Draw.io/XML and runtime visual review are required next; formal assets and page fallbacks remain gated until independent reviewer approval. Existing drawio, arch, SVG, and PNG artifacts were left unchanged and are not signoff evidence at this stage.
